transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: 57m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Alex, Priya, Samir, Leah (BristleCommerce)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, trimmed): Quick hosted API demo focused on how Redwood embeddings + reranker can improve search precision for product search. Covered: embeddings endpoint, rerank endpoint, Console demo for per-route metrics, and Optimize suggestions (batching & quantization). Agreed next steps: send pricing and sample configs; Bristle to share query set for pilot.

Topics: Hosted embeddings quality, rerank pipeline, prefix caching, latency vs cost trade-offs, security & data residency, pilot scope and timeline.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan with Redwood Inference, i'll hand to Maya our SE to run through the technical side. we have about an hour.
00:12 Alex: Hey thanks, we've been benchmarking some embeddings already but want to see a full rerank flow and how to integrate with our storefront.
00:20 Maya: cool, quick intro: we'll show how our hosted embeddings endpoint + the rerank endpoint can be used in a two-stage retrieval setup. we'll demo the Console for per-route latency/cost and then Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization.
00:34 Samir: quick note — currently we're on Elastic for retrieval and have a small in-house reranker that runs on CPU. latency is about 220ms per query and quality is mixed. goal is sub-150ms and better top-3 precision.
00:48 Maya: perfect. so first slide, architecture — sorry i'm sharing my screen, can everyone see the Console? (brief pause)
01:05 Leah: yeah we can see it. the per-route dashboard looks neat.
01:12 Maya: great. on Console you can pin a model version, see token-level cost and a heatmap for sequence lengths. that helps us pick an embeddings dim vs model family.
01:29 Jordan: one thing we often recommend is using a smaller dense embedding model for dense retrieval and then the rerank model for the top-K. customers often ask about using same model for both — possible but usually pricier.
01:44 Priya: when you say 'smaller model', do you mean lower dimension or quantized weights? what's the tradeoff?
01:52 Maya: both. lower-dim vectors reduce storage and nearest-neighbor cost. quantization reduces per-token compute on the GPU. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles by workload — e.g., 8-bit for retrieval embeddings and 4-bit for reranker in many cases.
02:10 Alex: any gotchas with recall dropping if we quantize embeddings?
02:15 Maya: small drop sometimes; Optimize shows a delta estimate based on evals. we also recommend hybrid recall: do dense ANN + fallback to sparse (BM25) for tail queries.
02:30 Jordan: i'm going to switch to a live demo — will run a simple pipeline: call embeddings endpoint, do a nearest neighbor lookup (we use an external vector DB in this demo), then call the /rerank endpoint to reorder the top 10.
02:44 Maya: note: our hosted rerank endpoint accepts JSON list of candidate documents and the user query, and returns a score + optional explain tokens.
03:00 Samir: that explain token thing, is it deterministic or a soft attribution?
03:05 Maya: it's an attention-based saliency — not a formal SHAP, but useful for triage.
03:14 03:20 Jordan: running the embeddings call now... pinging the hosted API from my laptop, simple curl example we provided earlier. (typing noises) response in 180ms, vector dim 1024.
03:42 Alex: 180ms is promising, is that measured from your location or from within the region?
03:47 Jordan: that's from my laptop in us-east, our Console shows regional breakdowns so you can see cross-region p99s. for production we'd recommend a region close to your users or a dedicated pool.
04:05 Priya: dedicated pool — that's Redwood Dedicated, right? any reason to choose Dedicated over hosted for a pilot?
04:12 Maya: for pilots, hosted is easier and faster. Dedicated beneficial when you need guaranteed throughput, isolated data, or specific GPU families. for your use case, start hosted, then move to Dedicated if traffic grows or you need lower jitter.
04:30 Alex: security — we need encryption at rest with our KMS and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. can you show where that appears?
04:37 Jordan: absolutely, in the Console under "Security" we list KMS integrations, audit log exports — i'll open the security slide.
04:50 Maya: two quick notes: for Private (VPC) deployments we can integrate with your KMS/HSM and keep model state in your VPC. Hosted keeps encrypted payloads but keys are managed by Redwood unless you bring-your-own-key via partner KMS.
05:12 Samir: do you support SSO SAML for team access?
05:15 Jordan: yes, SAML/SSO + RBAC and token scoping per-route.
05:22 Leah: ok demo continues?
05:25 Jordan: now i'll call the rerank endpoint with the top 10 candidates — payload size small. rerank returned in 95ms, rescored top-3 changed, pre-rerank precision@3 was 0.63, post-rerank 0.81 on this sample set.
06:02 Alex: those numbers are good, what was the model?
06:05 Maya: rerank model is a dedicated cross-encoder we host; in this example it's a distilled variant (we label it rnk-small-v2). it's tuned for ecommerce text and product attributes.
06:17 Priya: curious about cost per query — if embeddings + rerank both run, what's a ballpark?
06:22 Jordan: depends on model sizes and token counts. Console shows per-route cost; with small rerank + compact embeddings this demo maps to ~ $0.004 per query at current rates. we'll include a simple cost sheet.
06:40 Samir: we have some long product descriptions — will that blow up token costs?
06:44 Maya: longer contexts increase rerank cost. we do prefix trimming, KV cache for completion workstreams; for rerank we usually strip down to title + 2 key attributes + 64 tokens of description to limit tokens. Optimize can auto-suggest a trimming rule.
07:05 Alex: let's talk about evaluation — how do you measure and avoid regressions during model rollouts?
07:11 Maya: Console supports per-prompt eval sets, you can pin a model version and run A/B rollouts. we also surface quality regression alerts tied to a labeled prompt set.
07:30 Priya: can we test on our own queries before commit?
07:33 Jordan: yes, we can run a private eval on your golden set (Samir mentioned 100 cases) and show delta metrics before pilot.
07:45 Leah: curious about vector store recommendations — you mentioned you use an external DB in the demo; do you support managed vector indexes?
07:53 Maya: we don't force a specific store. many customers use Pinecone or FAISS in their infra; Redwood can optionally host a managed index or we can stream vectors to your existing DB. for pilots we typically recommend using your existing index for easier comparison.
08:15 Samir: latency targets — we need p95 < 150ms in EU region. realistic?
08:20 Maya: p95 < 150ms for embeddings+rerank is aggressive but feasible with proper routing: use a single model combo optimized for latency, regional endpoints, and small reranker. Dedicated pools will help stabilize p95.
08:36 Jordan: switching back to Console — here's Optimize's recommendation tab: suggests batching size 8 for our traffic pattern and enables prefix caching for repeated queries, could save ~25% token cost.
08:55 Alex: explain prefix caching — will it change results?
09:00 Maya: prefix caching caches prefix KV states used in streaming generation; for embedding+rerank it's less relevant, but for assistant flows it can reduce cost without changing deterministic scoring. for rerank we use static scoring so caching pertains mostly to candidate generation if you use a model to expand queries.
09:20 Priya: do you provide a sample rerank config for our infra?
09:24 Maya: yes — i'll paste a sample config to the chat after call: includes input normalization, candidate truncation, scoring thresholds, and fallback policy.
09:35 Jordan: quick question from me — what would you consider success for pilot?
09:40 Alex: 10% uplift in purchase conversion originating from search, p95 latency under 200ms, and ops being comfortable with integration work.
09:49 Jordan: that sounds tangible. we'll codify those in the pilot success criteria doc.
10:00 (long pause, typing)
10:18 Leah: does Redwood support partial rollbacks? if a model causes issues, can we revert?
10:22 Maya: yes, Console supports immediate rollbacks to previous pinned model and automatic fallback policy to a cheaper variant if errors spike.
10:34 Samir: we want to run some A/B tests on our site — can Redwood do traffic splitting?
10:38 Jordan: yes, per-route traffic split is supported and metrics are surfaced. you can split by percentage and target keys.
10:45 Priya: any recommended guardrails for online rerank? we have concerns about hallucination in generated explainers.
10:53 Maya: for rerank we keep it classification/regression style — model returns score, not freeform text. explainers are optional and trimmed. hallucination is mostly a concern for generation endpoints.
11:08 Alex: security follow-up — we'll need SOC2, ISO, encryption in transit + at rest, and contractual language around data retention. can you send legal & security docs?
11:15 Jordan: yes, i'll attach the SOC2 + encryption and our standard DPA.
11:22 Samir: technical detail — is rerank stateful? do you cache any user PII?
11:26 Maya: rerank is stateless per request. we don't persist user inputs in model state; logs can be configured to redact or forward to your SIEM.
11:36 Leah: ok, time check, about 15 minutes left — any last technical deep dives?
11:42 Priya: i'd like to see an end-to-end curl example that includes signed headers and a sample rerank payload.
11:47 Jordan: sure — paste briefly: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"blue running shoes"}' then call /v1/rerank with {"query":"blue running shoes","candidates":[{"id":1,"title":"Blue Run Shoe - 2025","desc":"lightweight..."},...] }
12:12 Samir: will share our dataset link after the call.
12:20 Jordan: recap: Jordan send pricing + security docs, Maya send rerank config + eval template, Bristle to upload query set, schedule pilot kickoff next week.
12:35 Alex: thanks all, that was useful. excited to try pilot.
12:40 (meeting fades; recording ends)
